meta.title: Research Agent — LSPRAI multi-role research assistant
meta.description: Planner, researcher, writer and reviewer agents work in sequence over your knowledge base, so every conclusion links back to its source.

hero.lede: Planner, researcher, writer and reviewer agents work in sequence: they search your knowledge base, write it up and check every citation.

constellation.label: Illustration of the four collaborating agent roles
constellation.answerText: The LSPR peak red-shifts as the surrounding refractive index rises, enabling label-free biosensing; the longitudinal mode of gold nanorods is usually more sensitive than nanospheres.

workflow.title: Four roles, one traceable research pipeline
workflow.lede: Complex questions are no longer written in one pass by one model. Each role does one job and hands it on; the reviewer sends problems back for revision.
workflow.planDesc: Understands the question and splits it into searchable sub-questions and an outline.
workflow.researchDesc: Searches the knowledge bases you selected and picks the relevant passages.
workflow.writeDesc: Writes from the evidence and cites a source for every conclusion.
workflow.reviewDesc: Checks each citation and claim and returns the draft for one revision if needed.
workflow.note: With a knowledge base connected and strict source mode on, comparison, review and summary questions switch to the four-role workflow automatically; open the answer's execution details to follow each role.

evidence.title: Every conclusion leads back to the source
evidence.lede: Each marker in an answer points to a specific passage in your knowledge base. Open it to see the text, page and position.
evidence.hybrid: Keyword and vector search run together, then a local reranker picks the most relevant passages.
evidence.locate: Citations resolve to the page and passage, with the source text highlighted.
evidence.honest: In strict source mode the assistant tells you when your sources do not support an answer instead of filling the gap.
evidence.demoQuestion: Why are gold nanorods better than nanospheres for refractive-index sensing?
evidence.demoAnswer: The longitudinal resonance of gold nanorods sits at longer wavelengths and responds more strongly to refractive-index changes
evidence.demoAnswerTail: ; the aspect ratio also tunes the resonance to the detection band.
evidence.demoSourceMark: the longitudinal plasmon resonance of gold nanorods lies at longer wavelengths and shows a higher sensitivity to the refractive index of the surrounding medium

knowledge.title: Your documents, properly read first
knowledge.lede: Upload PDF, Word and text notes. Parsing and indexing run locally, and every processing step is visible.

capabilities.title: A workspace built for long-running research
capabilities.tasks: Long tasks keep running after you leave; stop or add requirements at any time, and resume from checkpoints after a restart.
capabilities.memory: Knowledge bases are reused across your projects; chats, tasks and long-term memory stay per project, traceable, correctable and deletable.
capabilities.clarify: When information is missing the assistant asks you first and continues after you answer.
capabilities.tools: Connect your own MCP servers and skills; every call needs your approval.
capabilities.models: See the generation, embedding and rerank models in use and switch the generation model in chat.
capabilities.faq: Standard answers linked to alternative phrasings, with online editing, re-indexing and de-duplication.

final.title: Your next research question starts here.
final.lede: Upload your first document and put the research team to work.
